Issue_Name: Particle System with a very high particle budget
Individually_Recommended_Severity: Info (Warning only for explicit active-effect budget breach or measured overload)
Individual_Severity_Rationale: ParticleSystem.maxParticles is a maximum particle count, not proof of actual particle count or eagerly preallocated memory. A high cap may matter if the effect reaches it, but the cap alone does not prove GPU/CPU/memory overload.
Severity_Confidence: High for maxParticles cap; low for runtime cost inference
Required_Severity_Gate: Warning only when live/reachable effects exceed a project budget or profiler/device tests show a frame-time or memory regression. Do not infer preallocation from the cap alone.
Current_Description_Why: Max Particles reserves buffers up front and caps how much simulation and overdraw the system can generate. Large budgets are usually left over from tuning.
Rule_Specific_Claim_To_Prove: Whether a Particle System’s particle cap is actively approached and causes material cost in the target scene/build, rather than simply allowing a possible maximum.

External_Evidence_Limit: Effect cost depends on emission rate, lifetime, simulation space, collision, trails, renderer/material, screen coverage, overdraw, concurrency and hardware.
Project_Evidence_Still_Required: Capture emission/lifetime/actual live count, particle collision and trails, overdraw/frame debugger, VFX CPU/GPU frame timings, concurrent active systems and quality tiers.

Automation_Batch_Strategy: Group by shared ParticleSystem prefab/settings and quality tier; report total active upper bound plus observed live counts; do not create one review task per effect instance.

Issue_Name: static geometry not marked static
Individual_Severity_Rationale: Marking suitable objects static can enable batching or other precomputed data, but static flags have distinct meanings and can increase build data or cause incorrect behavior if moving objects are marked static. “Static” is not an all-or-nothing optimization switch.
Severity_Confidence: High for static flags; moderate for suitability
Required_Severity_Gate: Only propose flags required by a specific optimization and only for confirmed immovable content. A missing static flag alone is not a performance defect.
Current_Description_Why: Renderers that never move can be combined by static batching, contribute to occlusion culling and receive baked lighting. Without the static flags none of that applies.
Rule_Specific_Claim_To_Prove: Whether an object is permanently immovable and qualifies for one or more static systems that benefit this target project, without increasing cost or changing behavior.
External_Source_Audit_Status: Rule-specific official Unity 6.0 documentation/API page inspected; documented mechanism matched. Project-specific optimization impact is not established by the source.

Recommended_Fix_Mode: Info only; specific static-flag batch only with high-confidence immobility and per-feature eligibility
Automation_Batch_Strategy: Group by static flag type and asset/prefab. Do not change the Everything flag globally; use conservative per-feature policies and isolate scripted/moving objects.

Issue_Name: VideoClip is unsupported on WebGL
Individual_Severity_Rationale: The detector flags every VideoClip when target platform is WebGL, independent of whether the clip is reachable, included in the selected build or actually embedded through VideoPlayer.clip. The platform limitation is real but the detector’s scope is too broad for unconditioned Critical.
Severity_Confidence: High for Unity 6 WebGL limitation; medium for current project applicability
Required_Severity_Gate: Critical only for embedded VideoClip content referenced by required WebGL build content. Ignore clips for other targets, unused assets and WebGL paths that use VideoPlayer.url.
Current_Description_Why: Unity 6 does not support embedded VideoClip assets on WebGL. Web builds should use VideoPlayer.url with a browser-playable video hosted or delivered separately.
Rule_Specific_Claim_To_Prove: Unity 6 WebGL does not support embedded VideoClip playback through VideoPlayer.clip; WebGL video playback uses VideoPlayer.url and browser-supported media delivery.

What_Source_Supports: Unity documentation says embedded VideoClip is unsupported on WebGL and directs playback toward URL/browser delivery.
External_Evidence_Limit: A rule that emits per texture/video asset solely because the build target is WebGL may create noise for assets never used in the Web build or for URL-based video architecture.
Project_Evidence_Still_Required: Trace VideoPlayer.clip consumers from selected WebGL scenes/prefabs, inspect build-reachable assets, configured target profile and URL/browser-compatible media delivery.
